title: Raspberry macaron
subtitle: Pink French macarons with a sharp raspberry buttercream or ganache filling
excerpt: French macarons with a raspberry filling, shell made from almond flour, icing sugar, and aged egg whites, filled with a sharp raspberry buttercream or white chocolate raspberry ganache. The shells are naturally gluten-free. The keys are aged whites, precise folding, and full drying before baking.
sourceNotes: French macarons (not to be confused with macaroons) are a Paris patisserie staple. The meringue-based shell technique is documented in French confectionery tradition.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the assembled macarons in a single layer, then box them. Defrost for 1 hour at room temperature before serving. The shells soften slightly but remain good.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Macaron shells can be made 2 days ahead and stored in an airtight tin. Fill on the day or the day before serving.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: conventional oven; fan 130°C, macarons need steady heat with no hot spots

glossaryTerms.definition: The folding technique used to incorporate dry almond mixture into French macaron meringue. The aim is to deflate the meringue slightly until the batter flows from the spatula in a slow, thick ribbon. Too much macaronage and the shells spread flat; too little and they dome and crack.
The ruffled band that forms at the base of a properly made macaron shell during baking. Feet are a sign of correct batter consistency and adequate resting time before baking.

content.text: Raspberry macarons use the same shell as the classic French macaron, almond flour, icing sugar, and meringue, with a small amount of red or pink gel colouring added. The filling is a sharp raspberry buttercream or a white chocolate and raspberry ganache that contrasts with the almond sweetness of the shell.

attrs.prepNote: aged at room temperature for 24 hours (about 4 medium eggs)

content.text: Cook 150 g caster sugar with 45 ml water in a small saucepan to 118°C (soft-ball stage). While the syrup cooks, whisk 55 g of the aged egg whites to soft peaks. Pour the hot syrup in a thin stream into the egg whites while whisking constantly. Continue whisking until the meringue is stiff, glossy, and cooled to room temperature.
Combine the sifted almond flour and icing sugar with the remaining 55 g raw egg whites and the colouring. Stir to a rough paste. Fold the Italian meringue into the paste in three additions. The

is complete when the batter flows from the spatula in a slow, thick ribbon that disappears back into itself after about 10 seconds. Pipe 3.5 cm rounds onto parchment-lined trays. Bang the tray on the bench twice to pop surface bubbles.

Leave the piped shells to rest at room temperature for 45 to 60 minutes until a skin forms on the surface, touch lightly and the batter should not stick to your finger. Bake at 150°C (conventional) for 14 to 15 minutes. The shells should have formed feet and come away from the paper cleanly when cool. Leave to cool completely on the tray before filling.

Beat 150 g softened butter with 100 g icing sugar until pale. Fold in the strained raspberry jam. Pipe a small mound of filling onto the flat side of one shell, then press another shell on top. The macarons benefit from a few hours in the fridge before serving, the shells soften slightly and the flavour deepens.
